run.question: Search the 'app-183c-logs' index for ERROR level log messages. What error codes (format ERR-XXXX) appear in the logs?

report.summary: A query of the Elasticsearch index app-183c-logs for level=ERROR over the authorized window 2026-11-20T04:32:21Z to 2026-11-21T04:32:21Z returned 3 ERROR documents (total relation 'eq', value 3, not truncated). The three ERR-XXXX codes present are ERR-9463 (inventory-api, stock sync failed against an external inventory API returning 503, 2026-11-21T04:26:00Z), ERR-4058 (order-service, payment validation failed on invalid card number format, 2026-11-21T04:16:00Z) and ERR-7291 (payment-api, database connection timeout after 30s connecting to the primary database, 2026-11-21T04:11:00Z). These are three separate findings in three different services; the evidence does not tie them to one another or establish which is the cause of any incident. Only ERROR-level documents were requested and reviewed; non-ERROR documents in the index were not inspected.

claims.text: The index app-183c-logs exists with mappings error_code (keyword), level (keyword), message (text), service (keyword) and timestamp (date); the index listing reported 7 documents at query time.

The ERROR-level query on app-183c-logs over 2026-11-20T04:32:21Z to 2026-11-21T04:32:21Z matched 3 documents in total (relation 'eq'), all 3 returned, none omitted, shards failed 0, timed_out false; their timestamps span 2026-11-21T04:11:00Z to 2026-11-21T04:26:00Z.
Error code ERR-9463 appears in an ERROR log from service inventory-api at 2026-11-21T04:26:00Z: message 'Stock sync failed - ERR-9463: External inventory API returned 503'.
Error code ERR-4058 appears in an ERROR log from service order-service at 2026-11-21T04:16:00Z: message 'Payment validation failed - ERR-4058: Invalid card number format'.
Error code ERR-7291 appears in an ERROR log from service payment-api at 2026-11-21T04:11:00Z: message 'Database connection timeout - ERR-7291: Failed to connect to primary database after 30s'.

The inventory-api ERROR (ERR-9463) states an external inventory API returned 503, which points at that external dependency as a candidate cause for stock-sync failure; no evidence in this Run identifies the external API's owner, health or its own error signals, so this remains an unverified hypothesis.

The payment-api ERROR (ERR-7291) reports a 30s timeout connecting to the primary database, which points at the primary database or the network path to it as a candidate cause for payment-api failure; no database metrics, logs or spans were queried in this Run, so this is unverified.

The three ERROR entries belong to three distinct services (inventory-api, order-service, payment-api) with unrelated messages (upstream 503, card-number format validation, database connect timeout); the logs contain no shared error code or shared component linking them into a single fault chain.

gaps: The query covered only level=ERROR documents; the 4 remaining documents in app-183c-logs (index count 7 at query time) were not inspected, so whether any of them also carry an ERR-XXXX code in their message is unknown.
No time range outside 2026-11-20T04:32:21Z to 2026-11-21T04:32:21Z was queried, so whether these ERR-XXXX codes occurred before or after that window is unknown.

The three services named in the logs (inventory-api, order-service, payment-api) were not checked against Prometheus traces/RPC metrics, Kubernetes workload state or pod logs in this Run, so their health and the impact of these errors are unknown.
The external inventory API referenced by ERR-9463 and the primary database referenced by ERR-7291 were not identified or queried; their status is unknown.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so whether a deployment or configuration change preceded these errors cannot be verified.
next_steps: If the aim is triage, cross-check the three services named in the ERROR logs against their trace error spans and rpc_*_status_code metrics over the same window to see whether these log errors correspond to request failures.
Inspect pod logs and workload state for inventory-api, order-service and payment-api if the log index alone is insufficient, since app-183c-logs holds only 7 documents.
Widen the Elasticsearch window or add a query on the error_code field directly if entries outside the authorized window matter.
